about: Re-reads of the Storm Charles map: what changed since the first read (10 November, 23:38 to 23:48 UTC). Press headlines are evidence, quoted briefly with their source; IPMA's lines are facts read from IPMA. Not a forecast of ours.

at_the_authorities.label: fact
at_the_authorities.what: Correction (07:40Z): this entry first said nothing had changed at the authorities. IPMA had sent a CAP message at 07:16:30Z lowering Lisbon's wind warning to ORANGE, 09:00 to 21:00, gusts up to 120 km/h; the red rain stands. This re-read compared only IPMA's open data, which lagged the CAP message; the site's own record is the timeline row s-1111T0738 and data/weather/cap.json

rereads.observation_for_the_home_page: Between the two reads two live blogs changed their headline to a weaker or more southerly storm while IPMA's warnings for Lisbon stayed exactly the same. A reader of headlines and a reader of warnings now hold different pictures. This is idea 9 in practice: show the authority's unchanged line and the press's changed line side by side, each labelled and timed.
